title: Rehab after joint replacement
what: A physical therapist teaches you to move with your new joint: exercises for strength, flexibility, and walking. This helps the joint work better.
why: After a knee or hip replacement, usually from the first days after surgery.
duration: sessions usually last 30 to 60 minutes; the course usually lasts several weeks or months
tell_doctor: Which joint was replaced, and when
Other painful joints or back pain

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Loose clothes, shorts or trousers that roll up easily. Steady shoes with a back.

prepare.title: Pain relief
prepare.text: If your doctor prescribed a painkiller, you may be able to take it before the session. Ask your doctor.

prepare.title: Support
prepare.text: Bring the crutches or walker you use.

steps: The therapist checks the joint and measures its movement
You start with a gentle warm-up
You do exercises to bend and straighten the joint
Thigh and buttock muscles are strengthened
You practice walking, stairs, and getting up from a chair
Sometimes a cold pack is put on the joint at the end
feel: A pulling pain during exercises can happen. It should be bearable. You will be told how much is OK
After the session, tiredness and mild swelling
after: Do your home exercises every day
Cold and a raised leg reduce swelling
After a hip replacement, follow the position limits your doctor gives
Walk without support when your doctor allows
red_flags: Pain and swelling in the calf, or the leg feels hot
A fever over 38°C (100.4°F), redness, or discharge from the scar
Sudden pain, or the leg looks shorter or twisted: call emergency services
Sudden shortness of breath or chest pain: call emergency services

faq.a: Usually the main part takes 6 to 12 weeks, full recovery a few months.

faq.q: Can I exercise if it hurts?
faq.a: Mild pain during exercise happens. Strong pain is a reason to stop and tell your therapist.

reminders.text: Rehab session tomorrow. Bring comfortable clothes, shoes, and your crutches.
